conventions.convention: Systems use second-countable LCH groups, jointly Borel actions on standard Borel spaces, separable complex Hilbert spaces, and covariance U_g P(E) U_g⁻¹ = P(gE). PVM regularity is not part of the system definition.
Transitivity fixes a Borel equivariant identification with G/H for a closed subgroup H. AC supplies existence and uniqueness of the normalized homogeneous measure class.
The cocycle fields use the source variable: φ_g₁g₂(x) = φ_g₁(g₂x)φ_g₂(x). The original identity holds for each fixed pair almost everywhere; evaluation at eH occurs only after strict regularization.
The abelian spectral convention is π(n) = ∫χ(n)dP(χ), and the dual action is k·χ = χ composed with α_k⁻¹.
For coordinate translation U_teⱼ, momentum is P_j = Fourier⁻¹ M_2πξⱼ Fourier, U_teⱼ = exp(−itP_j), and the library Stone generator is T_j = −P_j.

R = Q[x₁,…,xₙ], deg x_i = 2; external shifts satisfy M(r)_d = M_d+r and internal shifts satisfy M{r}_d = M_d−r. F_i has degrees 0,1 and F_i⁻¹ has degrees −1,0. The negative differential uses the balanced root α_i = (−1)ⁱ⁻¹(x_i−x_i+1).
Normalized comparisons are unique homotopy classes with specified derived images, in internal degree zero. The relevant Hom space is Q; unrestricted graded endomorphisms of the unit form R.
Hecke normalization is q = v⁻², H_i = v(T_i+1), and v[X] = [X(1)]. Thus χ(F_i) maps to vT_i and χ(F_i⁻¹) to v⁻¹T_i⁻¹.

Chow relations use principal divisors on possibly singular integral subvarieties, with order given by differences of quotient lengths. Finite type schemes use finite cycles; merely locally finite type schemes use locally finite cycles and relations. For pure dimension n, A^p = A_n−p.
Projective bundles in the Chow formula parametrize line quotients of E and use ξ = c₁(O(1)); projective completions of normal vector bundles explicitly use the lines convention.
Refined Gysin uses the normal cone embedded in the pulled-back normal bundle after arbitrary base change; the base-changed immersion need not remain regular. Excess is the quotient N′/N₀.

K⁰ → K₀ is identified using finite locally free resolutions on regular quasi-projective finite type schemes. Coherent products use the transported product, equivalently alternating Tor, rather than ordinary tensor product.

GRR assumes AC, an algebraically closed field, nonsingular irreducible quasi-projective finite type source and target, and an H-projective morphism. Character and Todd series are rational and truncated above the dimension.

load_bearing.statement: Assume AC. For X locally of finite type over a field and E finite locally free of rank r ≥ 1, with quotient projective bundle π and ξ = c₁(O(1)), the map ⊕ᵢ₌₀ʳ⁻¹ A_d+i(X) → A_d+r−1(P(E)), (α_i) ↦ Σ ξⁱ∩π*α_i, is an isomorphism. Moreover π*(ξˢ∩π*α) = 0 for s < r−1 and π*(ξʳ⁻¹∩π*α) = α.

Assume AC. The operations c(Z,T,N) commute with every bivariant operation. For Z ⊂ Y ⊂ T and compatible virtual normal bundles in the exact sequence 0 → N_Z/Y → N_Z/T → N_Y/T|Z → 0, c(Z,T,N_Z/T) = c(Z,Y,N_Z/Y)c(Y,T,N_Y/T). For regular embeddings this gives (ji)! = i!j! after all base changes. A regular section of a smooth morphism gives s!p* = 1.

Assume AC. For a two-dimensional local domain A essentially of finite type over a field and f,g ∈ Frac(A)×, define ∂q(f,g) through normalization and norms of the DVR tame symbols. Then Σq ord_A/q(∂q(f,g)) = 0. The resulting rational-section relations establish first Chern descent, Cartier Gysin descent with support, and commutation of Cartier Gysins.

Assume AC. For a PVM P on a standard Borel X acting on a nonzero separable complex Hilbert space H, and a finite P-faithful Borel measure μ, there are a Borel multiplicity m:X → {1,2,…,∞} and a unitary W:H → ∫⊕ C^m(x)dμ with WP(E)W⁻¹ = M_1E for every Borel E. Finite P-faithful measures exist, and any two are mutually absolutely continuous.

Assume AC. For the second-countable LCH homogeneous-space data G,H,μ,s, separable K, and a Borel U(K)-valued cocycle whose law holds for each pair almost everywhere and whose dependence on g is continuous in local measure in the strong topology, there exist a strongly continuous σ:H → U(K) and Borel B with c(g,x) = B(gx)σ(s(gx)⁻¹gs(x))B(x)⁻¹ for every g and almost every x. This formula is a strict Borel cocycle; σ is unique up to unitary equivalence under Borel gauge changes.

Assume AC. For second-countable LCH abelian N, a strongly continuous unitary π on a separable Hilbert space, and a strongly continuous covariant action τ of a second-countable locally compact automorphism group K, there is a unique regular PVM P on the dual with π(n) = ∫χ(n)dP and τ(k)P(E)τ(k)⁻¹ = P(k·E). Irreducibility of the N⋊K representation implies ergodicity of this spectral measure class.
For 1 ≤ i ≤ n−2, F_i⊗F_i+1⊗F_i ≃ F_i+1⊗F_i⊗F_i+1 in Kᵇ(Rᵉ-grmod), with no grading shift. The proof gives two identity Gaussian pivots and a degreewise sign comparison of the surviving complexes.

For signed words t,u representing the same braid, the internal-degree-zero Hom in Kᵇ is one-dimensional over Q, and localization to the corresponding Dᵇ Hom is an isomorphism. The specified nonzero derived graph comparison has a unique lift γ_t,u; these lifts are mutually inverse homotopy equivalences.

Assume AC. On a regular quasi-projective scheme of finite type over a field, K⁰(X) → K₀(X) is an isomorphism. Every coherent sheaf has a finite locally free resolution, and its class corresponds to the resolution's alternating sum independently of the resolution. Regularity alone is not asserted to supply such global resolutions on arbitrary schemes.

Assume AC. For a proper morphism of schemes locally of finite type over a field, an integral cycle V pushes to [k(V):k(f(V))][f(V)] when image and source dimensions agree, and to zero otherwise. This descends to Chow groups, is functorial, satisfies flat base change, and gives f*[X] = n[Y] for finite flat constant-degree n maps between integral schemes of the same dimension.

Assume AC. For a closed immersion i:X → Y of nonsingular irreducible quasi-projective finite type varieties over an algebraically closed field, with normal bundle N, and E ∈ K⁰(X) = G₀(X), ch(i*E) = i*(ch(E)td(N)⁻¹). Equivalently ch(i*E)td(T_Y) = i*(ch(E)td(T_X)); the tangent relation is an exact sequence, not a bundle splitting.

concerns.concern: Proof 1.1 says that the pulled-back virtual normal bundle 'surjects onto the normal line of D with locally free kernel Q'. The supplied map is instead the conormal surjection N∨ → I_D/I_D². Dualizing gives 0 → N_D → N → Q → 0, and the excess factor uses this quotient Q. A global surjection N → N_D is not supplied. The commutation argument can be recovered by the correct dual sequence, but the displayed bundle direction is wrong. The complete comparison argument in [Stacks 42.54.8](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/0FBI) uses the dual of the conormal kernel.

The Statement says 'replacing N′ by N′₀ multiplies the operation by the top Chern operator of N′/N′₀'. Read literally, this reverses the relation. Proof 4.1 correctly establishes c(N′) = c_top(N′/N′₀) composed with c(N′₀); the smaller-bundle operation is not obtained by multiplying the larger one. State that identity explicitly. It agrees with [Stacks 42.54.3](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/0FBI).

seams_checked.note: The actual interface is def-weak-action-of-a-group-on-a-category. The owned coherent-action definition preserves the distinction between pairwise existence of isomorphisms and chosen compositors satisfying pentagon and unit axioms; it proves coherence separately.

This is contextual rather than a load-bearing item citation. The opened plane-curve definition and Bézout statement require algebraic closure and no common component. The owned projective-space example proves the Chow degree product and expressly withholds identification with the scheme-theoretic intersection cycle; it does not invoke plane Bézout over an arbitrary field.

The opened Reidemeister-III consumer quotes the exact generator degrees and maps in F5 and the no-shift braid relation and two-sided inverses in F6. Proof 3.1 and 6.1 explicitly account for generator inversion, shifts, balanced-root signs, rational units, and specialization of actual homotopy identities to the reduced ring.

The opened HHH generator definition has F(σ_i) ≅ F_i⁻¹{1} and F(σ_i⁻¹) ≅ F_i{−1}, with the B-term in degree zero. Its Proof 3.1 justifies reduced comparisons by specializing ambient homotopy identities using a common invariant average. The opened Koszul comparison retains the factor-two and balanced-root units and does not identify derived graph equivalence with homotopy equivalence.
